notes.summary: Biology is the biggest science area in GA, with 2–3 questions. Expect cell organelles, human body facts, vitamins and deficiency diseases, diseases and their causes, and basic classification.

concepts.title: The cell
concepts.body:
• Cell discovered by Robert Hooke (1665); nucleus by Robert Brown. Cell theory: Schleiden and Schwann.
OrganelleJob
Mitochondria'Powerhouse of the cell' — makes ATP
RibosomeProtein synthesis
Lysosome'Suicide bag' — digestive enzymes
ChloroplastPhotosynthesis (plants only)
NucleusContains DNA; controls the cell
Plant cells have a cell wall (cellulose), chloroplasts and a large vacuole; animal cells have centrioles.

concepts.title: Human body: key numbers
concepts.body:
FactAnswer
Bones in an adult206
Longest boneFemur (thigh)
Smallest boneStapes (middle ear)
Largest organSkin
Largest glandLiver
'Master gland'Pituitary
Insulin made byPancreas (beta cells of islets of Langerhans)
Life of a red blood cellAbout 120 days
Normal body temperature37 °C (98.6 °F)
The heart has 4 chambers: two atria above, two ventricles below. Blood groups were discovered by Karl Landsteiner; O− is the universal donor and AB+ the universal recipient.

concepts.title: Vitamins and deficiency diseases
concepts.body:
VitaminDeficiency disease
ANight blindness
B1 (thiamine)Beriberi
B3 (niacin)Pellagra
B12Pernicious anaemia
CScurvy (bleeding gums)
DRickets (children)
KBlood does not clot properly
Fat-soluble vitamins: A, D, E, K. Water-soluble: B and C. Iodine deficiency causes goitre; iron deficiency causes anaemia.

concepts.title: Diseases and their causes
concepts.body:
CauseDiseases
BacteriaTuberculosis, cholera, typhoid, tetanus, diphtheria
VirusPolio, measles, rabies, chickenpox, dengue, AIDS
ProtozoaMalaria (Plasmodium, spread by female Anopheles mosquito)
FungiRingworm, athlete's foot
Dengue is spread by the Aedes mosquito. Classification: Five-kingdom system by R.H. Whittaker; binomial naming by Carolus Linnaeus.

example.q: Which organelle is called the 'powerhouse of the cell'?
steps: Energy (ATP) is made by cellular respiration

varieties.name: Human body
varieties.how: Recall the key-number table and the path of blood through the heart.

example.q: Which is the largest gland in the human body?

varieties.name: Vitamins and diseases
varieties.how: Use the vitamin table and classify each disease by its cause (bacteria / virus / protozoa / fungi).

example.q: Scurvy is caused by deficiency of which vitamin?
steps: Scurvy: bleeding gums, found in sailors without fresh fruit

tips: Vitamin chain: A-night blindness, B1-beriberi, C-scurvy, D-rickets, K-clotting.
Bacterial diseases often asked: TB, cholera, typhoid, tetanus, diphtheria ('TCT-TD').
Malaria is caused by a protozoan, not a virus or bacterium; the mosquito only carries it.
traps: Largest organ is skin, but largest gland is liver — options mix them.
Male Anopheles mosquitoes do not spread malaria; only females bite for blood.
Vitamin K helps blood clot; it is not linked to vision (that is vitamin A).

questions.q: Which organelle is known as the 'powerhouse of the cell'?
questions.solution:
Mitochondria carry out cellular respiration and produce energy as ATP.
Memory hook: Mighty-chondria = the mighty power plant.

questions.q: Night blindness is caused by deficiency of:
questions.solution:
Vitamin A is needed for the light-sensitive pigment in the retina; its lack causes night blindness. Carrots are a good source.
Memory hook: A for 'Aankh' (eye).

questions.q: How many bones are there in the body of an adult human?
questions.solution:
An adult has 206 bones. A newborn has about 300; many fuse as the child grows.
Memory hook: babies start with about 300 bones; fusing brings it down to 206.

Malaria is caused by the protozoan Plasmodium and spread by the bite of the female Anopheles mosquito.
Memory hook: P for Plasmodium, P for Protozoan.

questions.q: The smallest bone in the human body is the:
questions.solution:
The stapes (stirrup) in the middle ear is the smallest bone. The femur (thigh) is the longest.
Memory hook: Stapes is shaped like a tiny stirrup in your ear.

questions.q: Insulin is produced by which organ?
questions.solution:
Insulin is made by the beta cells of the islets of Langerhans in the pancreas. Its lack causes diabetes.
Memory hook: 'Islets in the Pancreas sea' produce insulin.

questions.q: Which chamber of the human heart pumps oxygenated blood to the whole body through the aorta?
questions.solution:
The left ventricle pumps oxygen-rich blood into the aorta. It has the thickest muscular wall because it pushes blood to the whole body.
Memory hook: the Left ventricle is the Largest pump — thickest wall, sends blood to the whole body.

questions.q: Which of the following diseases is caused by a bacterium?
questions.solution:
Typhoid is caused by the bacterium Salmonella typhi. Measles, polio and chickenpox are viral diseases.
Memory hook: Bacterial set 'TCT-TD': TB, Cholera, Typhoid, Tetanus, Diphtheria.
